architecture: ThingsBoard-shaped telemetry -> Raspberry Pi -> Modbus/TCP -> OpenPLC -> ValveCommand
claim_boundary: Conclusions apply to this laboratory testbed and evaluated files; not universal validation for all PAMSIMAS/OT environments.

findings.statement: Baseline cross-layer ODO integrity rate was 100.000%; all-fields cross-layer rate was 100.000%.
findings.title: Baseline cross-layer integrity

findings.statement: Raspberry Pi read availability was 100.000% and OpenPLC read availability was 100.000%.
findings.title: Baseline acquisition availability

findings.statement: OpenPLC logic consistency rate was 100.000%; valve output agreement with the legitimate source was 100.000%.
findings.title: Baseline controller behaviour

findings.statement: 6 record(s) showed OpenPLC ODO Meter equal to the configured attack value while the Raspberry Pi source sent a different legitimate value. Network write events were available and correlated.
findings.title: ODO Meter cross-layer integrity violation

findings.statement: Controller operational impact was observed in 6 record(s). This metric compares the actual valve output with the output expected from the legitimate Raspberry Pi source.
findings.title: Controller impact on valve output

findings.statement: PLC logic consistency was 94.118%. A high rate means OpenPLC correctly applied its control rules to the value it received, even when that value differed from the legitimate source.
findings.title: OpenPLC controller logic remained internally consistent

findings.statement: Raspberry Pi read availability was 100.000%; OpenPLC read availability was 73.913%. Availability of acquisition can remain high while process-data integrity is violated.
findings.title: Acquisition availability during treatment

findings.statement: Stable recovery was confirmed at 2026-07-28T11:52:00.541Z after 3 consecutive normal records.
findings.title: Stable recovery observed

limitations: The current source is ThingsBoard-shaped hardcoded/mock telemetry until the STM32 and live ThingsBoard integration are completed.
The Valve field from ThingsBoard is treated as observed field feedback; ValveCommand is the OpenPLC controller output.
Collector polling may be faster than sender publication, so duplicate source_sequence observations are expected and are not automatically classified as replay.
Acquisition availability does not by itself prove physical water-service availability.
